text: The rwb-integration login, the element names of the append command, of the P1 EFS and contact reads and of the five fact answers, the bodies of the two admin operations and the shape of the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task are taken as follows. The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02), granted on schema rwb_integration only, its name supplied by the ACE DB story of the service and never written in a story or a value. The append command carries caseId, eventCode, channel, direction, occurredAt, sourceSystem, contactKey, fromHolderRef, toHolderRef, treatmentId, proceedsId, deliveryStatus, externalRef and idempotencyKey. The append answers 201 with an entry reference, 200 with the same reference for a key already held, 409 for a conflicting key, 422 for an invalid command and 503 when the store is unavailable. The admin list answers the delivery id, the event type, the consumer, the status, the attempt count, the next attempt time, the last error code, the delivered time, the task id and the page envelope, and the resend answers the same delivery with status PENDING and attempt count 0. The task carries the delivery id, the consumer, the event type, the failure class and the owner role RW-PLATADM.
why: DP-02 fixes one login per service and the legacy story names the writer interfaces only; the FSD and the TSD give the tables, the states and the rights but no wire shape. Without element names the mapper, the client and the fakes cannot be built, and the names used here are the element names of the legacy LedgerEntryCommand and of the TSD P2 v3 T3.1 columns, so no business value is invented.
read: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json rulings on interaction, processed_event, outbox_delivery and idempotency_key; legacy RWB-E2-034 sections 11 to 13; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-01, DP-02 and DP-18
applied_in: 3 Preconditions; 7 AC8; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.2; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages

text: The per-type mapping of the entry fields is taken as follows. TreatmentApproved gives an OFFER entry with the treatment id as its link and the event time as its occurred time. NoticeDispatched gives a LETTER entry with delivery status SENT and the barcode as its external reference. NoticeDelivered gives a LETTER entry with delivery status DELIVERED and the barcode as its external reference. InstructionIssued gives a HANDOVER entry with channel PORTAL, direction OUTBOUND, the case holder before the move as the from reference and PARTNER:<partnerCode> as the to reference. PartnerResultSubmitted gives a PARTNER_RESULT entry with channel PORTAL and direction INBOUND. ProceedsMatched gives a PAYMENT entry with the proceeds id as its link. An EFS action row gives a CONTACT entry with source system EFS and the channel of the EFS ledger outcome list. Every other entry has source system WORKBENCH. The event time is the time the event says the interaction happened, carried unchanged and never replaced by the time of receipt. The event codes are the legacy codes and are sent character for character.
why: The legacy BR1, BR2 and BR4 fix the codes, the channels, the directions and the source system but not which payload element fills each field, and the payloads belong to five other services. The occurred time is the one field the timeline order depends on (BR9 of the legacy story), so it must be stated rather than left to each mapper.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 BR1, BR2, BR4, BR9 and AC1 to AC4; FSD P2 v3 A2.7; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 for the producers of the seven types
applied_in: 8 Business rules BR1, BR3 and BR4; 12.4; 13 Solution plan
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of the five fact contracts at the contract review
impact: The legacy behaviour is kept: one entry per event, one code per event type, the contact point as a reference and the occurred time of the channel, never the receipt time.

text: The retry policy of a ledger delivery is 1 minute before attempt 2, 10 minutes before attempt 3 and, where a fourth interval is configured, 1 hour, with an attempt limit of three, and the intervals are rows of the environment configuration and not code. After the third failed attempt the delivery moves to EXCEPTION with the last error code and raises the task RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY for role RW-PLATADM. A 4xx of the append other than 409 is non-retryable and parks the delivery at once; a 5xx, a timeout and an unresolvable case are retryable and take the three attempts.
why: The legacy story of this module fixes three attempts and the task for RW-PLATADM and the retry windows of 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour; the FSD fixes 5 and 15 minutes for the WIN outbound file only; neither applies to this consumer as a stated rule, so the intervals are an assumption and a configuration row.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 AC7, AC8 and BR8; FSD P2 v3 A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01 and A2.7.3; TSD P2 v3 T4 and T3.2; Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-09
applied_in: 8 Business rules BR6; 9 State transitions; 12.5; 13 Solution plan
confirm: Solution architect and the platform event owner at the contract review; the values are confirmed per environment by the DevOps lead
impact: No delivery is lost and none is parked before its third attempt; the intervals are tuning values and a change of interval needs no code change.

The intake slice is a reading of the higher ruling over those documents and has to be stated once so that four teams do not each build a ledger writer.

text: The published contract is taken as follows. Each of the seven consumed types is a CloudEvents 1.0 message keyed by its case id where a case exists, with the dedupe key <EV-nn>:<business key>:v1 for the six business events (treatment id, notice id, instruction id, proceeds id) and EFS:<efs_record_key> for an EFS row; a message without the envelope, without a business key or of an eighth type is routed to .dlt with an alert. The append is one operation, create-only and idempotent on the key, called before the inbox row is marked so that a replay returns the same entry reference; a 409 is treated as success. The delivery states are PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION, the attempt limit is three, and only a delivery in EXCEPTION may be resent, to PENDING with attempt count 0. The two admin operations are the re-based forms of API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 on the base /api/recovery/integration/v1, with Platform administration R and U, an Idempotency-Key on the resend and a 409 for a delivery not in EXCEPTION or an event whose workflow is already running.
why: The FSD gives two example dedupe keys, the TSD gives the four states and the rights, and the legacy story gives the three attempts; the business key of each type, the ordering of the append and the inbox, the legal state moves and the bodies of the two operations are not stated anywhere. A contract cannot be faked without them.

applied_in: 7 AC1 to AC6; 8 Business rules BR2 to BR7; 11 Data; 12.1 to 12.4

text: The fakes are taken as follows: the rwb-source-data fake answers the append with 201, the same reference on a repeat, 409, 503 and one slow answer, the EFS read with three rows (listed, unlisted and not on a case) for business date 2026-12-14, and the contact read with one hit and one 404; the rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment fakes answer one hit and one 404 each; the rwb-access fake grants and refuses Platform administration; the Kafka stubs hold one message per type, one duplicate per type, one malformed envelope and one eighth type. Every fake is compared with the document by a drift test that fails the merge, and a fake answer outside the declared shape is a defect. No statement of this service reads another service's table, a ledger table or an ACE view, and no foreign key leaves rwb_integration.

text: The deployment values are taken as follows. Two consumer groups are deployed: the ledger intake group on rwb.treatment.events.v1, rwb.comms.events.v1, rwb.partner.events.v1 and rwb.payment.events.v1, and the EFS read group on rwb.source-data.events.v1, both with an offset reset policy of earliest, a commit after the inbox row is marked and no assignment to a topic of this service. The delivery retry scan runs on its own interval and reads the deliveries where the status is PENDING or RETRYING and the next attempt is due. The lag threshold of each consumed topic, the exception queue count threshold, the append failure rate threshold and the stuck-run threshold of the EFS read step are environment values. The build ID is the one the workflow kit supplies for the release commit and worker versioning is enabled. The synthetic fixtures of the smoke run are owned by the DevOps team of the release and are created in DEV and SIT only.
why: The platform rule names topics, the task queue and the schema and gives no group, no offset rule, no threshold and no build ID format; the job map gives only the one-minute relay. An operator cannot act on a threshold that does not exist, so the values are fixed per environment and listed here rather than in code.

text: The observability of the deployment is taken as follows. The five dashboard series are consumer lag by group and partition, deliveries in RETRYING, deliveries in EXCEPTION, append answers by class and the EFS read summary counts, each with the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions. The three runbook entries are a lagging consumer group, a parked delivery and a missing EFS run. The build ID format is the release commit identifier supplied by the workflow kit, and the versioning policy is the platform default: a new build takes new workflows while the old build drains. No series, alert payload or runbook entry carries a case identifier beyond the delivery reference, a contact point, an amount or a decoded payload.
